findings.reason: the reader should resolve the phase directory through the same declared-store addressing the catalogue will own (or state that it mirrors those names only until `jt-60sa.json` lands), so the phase-to-directory map stays with the catalogue rather than being retyped in a figure script.
findings.text: the plan hardcodes the phase directories `OP1/`/`OP2/` under `JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR` and builds `{phase}/{ids}.nc` itself, re-deriving store addressing that already has an owner: `imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py` `resolve_description_store_root` resolves a declared store root and `imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py` `_NetCDFStoreArrays.read` addresses `{map dir}/{ids}.nc` for the static-over-map layout the `jt60sa-machine-map` catalogue is about to declare — two places naming the same phase directories will drift when the catalogue lands

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v5 §1 has the reader load jt-60sa.json (landed ef6895dd), take the root from description_store_root_path() and join each catalog.maps name, the static-over-map addressing transform_engine applies; the stale 'serves only mast' reason is removed

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the substantial behaviour (a phase's store to drawable families for coils, vessel, wall, flux loops and probes) sits behind one reader and one cross-section function in `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py`, which §2 extends rather than re-reading the store; the added `imas_ambix/plot_style.py` is a small, honest surface (named colour roles, an apply function, one shared direct-label helper), not a spread of wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan names the phase directories `OP1/` and `OP2/` itself, but those are the JT-60SA map names the machine-map plan lands as `imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/jt-60sa.json` and that `imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py` `resolve_description_store_root` plus `transform_engine.py` `_NetCDFStoreArrays` use to address exactly this store.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 adds one module and states in its own text that it "retires nothing" because `imas_ambix/` holds no plotting style code, and that the inline-styling scripts stay as they are, so the added surface is accounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites a specific 2026-10-06 search of `imas_ambix/data/`, `imas_ambix/gs/` and `scripts/`, naming `description_reader.read_geometry_table`, `load_packaged_machine_map`, `eddb.channel_path`/`channel_time_path`/`UNIT_ATTR`, `VirtualZarrView`, `MachineGeometryService.operator()`, `geometry_export.build_geometry_fields_from_table` and `scripts/validate_mast_geometry.py`, and gives a reason for rejecting each; no existing raw-store reader exists to reuse, so it is not rebuilding one.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two layers the plan adds are each justified in its own text: the store read is raw `imas.DBEntry` because `read_geometry_table` would transform what the figure must show as converter output, and `plot_style.py` is the repository's first colour assignment (nothing to extend or merge) whose direct-label helper §2 and §3 share.
